title: Pickleball paddles: sizing a hot market
prompt: Our client is a sporting goods brand that wants to launch a line of pickleball paddles. Estimate the annual US market for pickleball paddles, in dollars.

clarifying_answers.objective: Size the market to decide whether a paddle line is worth launching.
clarifying_answers.scope: Paddles only, not balls, shoes, or court fees.

hidden_facts.fact: About 20 million Americans played pickleball at least once last year.

hidden_facts.hint: types of players, how often people play, or core vs casual
hidden_facts.fact: About 25% are core players who play 8 or more times a year. The rest are casual players.

hidden_facts.hint: how often people buy a paddle
hidden_facts.fact: Core players buy about 1 new paddle a year. Casual players buy one about every 4 years.

hidden_facts.hint: paddle prices or what players spend
hidden_facts.fact: Core players spend about $120 per paddle. Casual players spend about $40.

math_answers.question: How many paddles are bought each year (in millions)?
math_answers.formula: players_m * core_pct / 100 * core_buys_per_year + players_m * (100 - core_pct) / 100 / casual_years_per_paddle

math_answers.question: What is the annual market in dollars?
math_answers.formula: players_m * core_pct / 100 * core_buys_per_year * core_price + players_m * (100 - core_pct) / 100 / casual_years_per_paddle * casual_price

ideal_structure: Players x paddles bought per player per year x price
Different replacement rates and prices per segment
recommendation: The market is about $750M a year. Core players are only 25% of players but spend $600M of it (80%), so the client should launch a premium paddle aimed at core players, selling through clubs and online.
common_mistakes: Assuming everyone buys a paddle every year
